# nocthost_server (Resource)

A NoctHost cloud server, billed by the hour from the prepaid balance. Creating it deploys a real server (`POST /servers`) and waits until it is `ACTIVE`; destroying it deletes the server (billing stops the same hour) and waits until it is gone. Changing anything except `label` replaces the server.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nocthost_server" "web" {
  label       = "web-1"
  provider_id = "hetzner"
  plan_id     = "vc2-1c-2gb" # Starter: 1 vCPU, 2 GB RAM
  region_id   = "fra"
  os_id       = 1743 # Ubuntu 22.04
  password    = var.root_password
  ssh_key     = file("~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub")

  timeouts {
    create = "20m"
    delete = "10m"
  }
}

variable "root_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

output "web_ip" {
  value = nocthost_server.web.ipv4
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `label` (String) Server name, also used as the hostname. Latin letters, digits, dot, dash and underscore, up to 64 characters. Can be changed in place.
- `plan_id` (String) Size to deploy. The standard sizes work on every cloud: `vc2-1c-1gb` (Micro), `vc2-1c-2gb` (Starter), `vc2-2c-4gb` (Standard), `vc2-4c-8gb` (Pro), `vc2-6c-16gb` (Beast), `vc2-8c-32gb` (Titan), `vc2-16c-64gb` (Colossus), `vc2-24c-96gb` (Leviathan). GPU sizes come from the `nocthost_gpu_plans` data source; all sizes and prices are on https://nocthost.com/pricing.
- `region_id` (String) Region (city) code, for example `ams`. See the `nocthost_regions` data source.

### Optional

- `app_slug` (String) One-click app to install instead of a plain OS (Vultr only). Conflicts with `os_id`.
- `os_id` (Number) Operating system ID from the catalog (default Ubuntu 22.04, `1743`). Conflicts with `app_slug`.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Root password: 12 to 72 Latin characters with at least three of lowercase, uppercase, digits and symbols, no spaces. Required by the API for almost every image. It is stored in Terraform state, so protect your state.
- `provider_id` (String) Cloud backend: `vultr`, `digitalocean`, `hetzner`, `linode` and others listed by the `nocthost_providers` data source. If omitted, the API uses its default backend (`vultr`); set it explicitly for predictable plans.
- `ssh_key` (String) Public SSH key installed for root at first boot (the whole line, starting with `ssh-ed25519`, `ssh-rsa` or `ecdsa-sha2-nistp256`).
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `access_type` (String) How to log in: `ssh` or `rdp` (Windows).
- `created_at` (String) Creation time (RFC 3339).
- `hourly_price` (Number) Price per hour in USD.
- `id` (String) Server ID.
- `image` (String) Installed OS or app, as a readable name.
- `ipv4` (String) Public IPv4 address.
- `status` (String) Server status: `PROVISIONING`, `ACTIVE`, `STOPPED`, `SUSPENDED`, `ARCHIVED`, `DESTROYING`, `DESTROYED` or `ERROR`.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing server by its ID (shown in the dashboard URL and by GET /servers).
terraform import nocthost_server.web <server-id>
```
